txt: She has fallen silent.
She shifts in her seat awkwardly.
The woman has grown silent. She draws shallow breaths.
The young woman stands and looks behind her. The shot has flown over her head -- crashing a small pane of the glass window behind her.
There's silence. The smallest of smiles.
"A bit much? What are you talking about? That's what my grandma told me, okay?"
"An autopsy? Wow. Sure, keep them." She hands you the rubber gloves. "I have another pair."
"Anything else?" The girl watches you rub your sides for warmth.
"As you *probably* know, there's a corpse hanging from a tree there. It smells pretty bad. So I have to take breaks."
"Ask me a normal question or leave me alone."
"Can you tell me when you've taken him away then. Because I'm sort of waiting for *that*."
"Do not think your *failed suicide attempt* will win you any pity from these men -- do not expect them to forget it soon either."
"Do not think your *failed suicide attempt* will win you any pity from these men. Do not expect them to forget it either."
"Down...?" The gardener straightens her back. "Do you mean the body is finally gone?"
"Excuse me?" She doesn't understand.
"Go easy on that stuff. It gave me a terrible headache."
"Gone to heaven?" A quick smile. "Thank you, officer. Looks like I'll get mint in the ground by April."
"Hello again, officer. How are things?"
"I am pleased to meet you too, officer."
"I can't believe it's snowing again..." The young woman resting by the wheelbarrow sighs.
"I don't know anything about that either. As I said, I didn't write it."
"I don't know... the abandoned kind? It used to gather every spring, but there's nothing to do there now. Just drug addicts."
"I don't know..." She looks around. "Whatever's on the radio I guess. What does this have to do with snow, or gardening in March?"
"I don't know..." She looks around. "Whatever's on the radio?"
"I have a greenhouse in the yard there." She gestures over her shoulder. "I've been trying to get some work done..."
"I like the city at night. Don't you?" She looks into the darkness and smiles again.
"I'll be okay... I'll be..." She puts her bloody hand on her heart and starts shaking.
"I'm a night hawk, what can I say?" She flashes a smile.
"I'm glad to hear that." A quick smile. "Thank you, officer. Looks like I'll get mint in the ground by April."
"I'm okay with it. Was there something else?"
"I'm okay... I'm okay..." The woman grabs her left side. She's down. Her white shirt soaks a blood red around her abdomen. She gasps for air.
"I'm okay... I'm okay..." The woman staggers backward, crouches, then grabs her left side. Her white shirt soaks a blood red around her abdomen and she gasps for air.
"I'm working."
"If you don't have anything normal to say I had something I needed to think about."
"In Martinaise, sir. In the city of Revachol..." She looks around, thinking what else to say. "This intersection is called Roundabout North."
"In heaven?" A quick smile. "Thank you, officer. Looks like I'll get mint in the ground by April."
"Is that so?" Her face remains expressionless as she shrugs. "I don't know anything about that. Must be a misunderstanding."
"Is there?"
"It felt like springtime just a few days ago..."
"It is, because he sent you to harass me, didn't he? You shouldn't listen to him." She points to the defaced sign above her on the corner. "It was probably him, who wrote that."
"It is, because he sent you to harass me. He's playing you." She shakes her head. "He hates the police, okay? A lot of people do around here."
"It was clear just an hour ago..."
"It's just water..." She looks at the water, squinting. "No, actually, I think they call it the Martinaise Inlet. There are some islands in the bay, but they're hard to reach."
"It's raining again..." The young woman resting by the wheelbarrow sighs.
"It's there." She points north. "In the yard, right through the hole in the fence."
"Just coast. There's a little fishing village there... and a fish market. But that got closed down ages ago."
"Like gone-gone?" The girl repeats, her face beaming with appreciation.
"Maybe you shouldn't be. I mean... you do your job, but that kid is beyond help. And he certainly won't help *you*." She shakes her head.
"Me? I'm just a gardener."
"Mhmh." She looks at her wheelbarrow, where the snow is slowly melting.
"Nitrogen and sulphur mostly." She points to the sky. "And whatever factories and aerostatics exhale too I guess."
"No problem." She nods, brushing a fleck of soil off her cheek.
"No, of course not! I don't understand what this is about..." She looks towards the yard and her expression clears.
"Of course he's racist. Look at how fat he is."
"Of course, I won't hold you back." She wipes her brow with the canary yellow glove.
"Of course. What can I help you with?"
"Of course. Where to?"
"Oh that..." She points north. "That's right there, in the yard."
"Oh, that must be the woman on the giant boat." She points northwest. "There's one docked on the pier. It arrived a couple of weeks ago. It's very hard to miss."
"Oh. Okay." She doesn't quite know what to say. "Thanks for keeping me in the know, sir."
"Oh... right." She scratches her cheek. "But not from the yard. I understand."
"Oh... right." She scratches her cheek. "Can you tell me when you've taken him away then?"
"Oh?" She cranes her neck. "Well, I didn't write it there. I'm just sitting here."
"Okay, well, I didn't," she leans back, shoulders relaxing.
"Okay," she replies, shoulders relaxing.
"Okay." She straightens her back.
"Okay."
"See you around, officer."
"Sir, it was *implied* in your question."
"Snow has nutrients in it -- helps everything green up in the spring. At least that's what my grandma always told me." She smiles shyly.
"Some shops and a bridge. The canal bridge leads to the coast, but it's broken, I think? Some kind of accident probably."
"Sure -- I'm done with it." She takes a small capsule out of her breast pocket and hands it to you.
"Sure -- I'm done with them." She takes a small capsule out of her breast pocket and hands it to you.
"Sure thing." She narrows her eyes.
"Sure, keep them. I have another pair." She hands you the rubber gloves with no visible annoyance.
"Thank you." She smiles politely. "My head is about to explode from all the salts I've had to inhale."
"The RCM in Martinaise?" The young woman looks up at you. "What can I help you with?"
"The harbour gates. Some kind of commotion, I think? I don't follow the local politics." She shrugs. "A Frittte store too."
"The kid did this, right? The red-haired rat? Can't say a sentence without *f****t* or *kipt*... He's always giving me trouble."
"There's the pier, the Capeside apartment buildings. Some more tenements... Not a lot, really."
"They... they didn't..." The woman holds on to her side, teeth rattling.
"Uh... I'm gonna say no."
"We don't see a lot of police around here, that's all."
"We're in Martinaise, sir." She looks around. "This intersection is called... Roundabout North, I think."
"Well uh..." She points to her wheelbarrow, surprised at the question. "This might be the last snow we get. At least I hope so..."
"Well... as you *probably* know, there's a corpse hanging from a tree there. It smells pretty bad. So I have to take breaks."
"What do you mean?"
"What does that mean?" She doesn't flinch.
"Wild Pines? You mean the company woman?"
"Yes, I'm black, how many times are you gonna say that?"
"Yes. I'm tired."
"Yes." She looks relieved. "It smells pretty bad, so I have to take breaks."
"You're back."
